floor_history.headline: Honest floor 17 -> 9: the 3 missing insns were cse forwarding the D_80101E60 reload; an aggregate (BLKmode) store of the D_80101E6C/D_80101E70 record flushes cse's memory table in pure C and restores

Floor 9 -> 2 and build_insns 78 -> 79 == target: all 79 instructions now match in opcode AND register; the residual 2 is two relocation ADDENDS (D_80101E60+12/+16 vs splat's D_80101E6C/D_80101E70) tha

frontier.hypothesis: The link-identity claim for the two relocation addends holds, so retiring the 8 regfix rules yields a full-build SHA1 == oracle and the function is byte-matched.
frontier.mechanism: GNU ld resolves an o32 R_MIPS_HI16 using the addend of the following R_MIPS_LO16, and 0x80101E60+12/+16 are exactly D_80101E6C/D_80101E70. With rules enabled the score is 4, so the 8 reorder/subst rules at regfix.txt:79-95 must be deleted first; regfix.txt and the retire verb are outside a grind session's surface.
frontier.next_probe: OPERATOR: run the engine's `retire func_80036FD4` (deletes those 8 rules, full-build SHA1-verifies, auto-rolls-back on mismatch). If SHA1 == 62efab4f73f992798c43e8c730aa43baa10bb4fa the claim holds; if it auto-rolls-back the claim is refuted, the residual is real, and the function returns to the queue with that measurement banked.

frontier.hypothesis: The committable spelling of the record is a single struct declaration in include/code6cac.h replacing the per-word externs, and it is score-neutral for this function.
frontier.mechanism: The emitted relocation addends are identical whether the record comes from a header declaration or from the in-function `(ReplayCamRec *)&D_80101E60` cast, so the cast is only a probe spelling. But D_80101E60/E62/E64/E68/E6A/E6C/E70/E74 are referenced from other files, and unifying them into one object changes their mutual aliasing, which can move other functions' codegen.
frontier.next_probe: OPERATOR/owner-scope: introduce the record type + declaration in include/code6cac.h, convert every use site to member accesses, and full-build SHA1-verify. Confirm this function's sandbox --disable all stays at 2 with identical bytes, then run the fresh layer-2 cheat-reviewer on the resulting body.

frontier.hypothesis: The sibling replay_camera_Init (code6cac_b2_post.c:242) is closable by the same two levers and would be freed by the same header record.
frontier.mechanism: It has the identical store/reload/pair-store shape at the same addresses and still carries `register asm("$7")` / `asm("$8")` pins plus the same `asm volatile("" ::: "memory")` barrier — i.e. it is paying cheats for exactly the cse-flush and schedule-position effects that the shared-base record buys for free. NOTE it writes the second word from D_8008EC38 rather than from SpecialCam, so the aggregate copy is NOT the same statement; only the base-sharing lever transfers.
frontier.next_probe: Out of scope for func_80036FD4. When that function reaches the queue top, apply the shared-base record to its D_80101E60 accesses and measure whether the two pins and the barrier can be dropped.
